short.q: State two lessons from the story of Stephen.
short.answer: Be brave; forgive; trust God.

short.q: Describe how Stephen died.
short.answer: The people were furious at his message, dragged him out of the city and stoned him. He prayed for God to receive his spirit and to forgive them.
short.working: 1 mark for anger, 1 for stoning, 1 for prayer.

short.q: Give three reasons why children should not join ungodly groups.
short.answer: They lead to wrong; they can harm us; they pull us from God and family; they ask for secrets.

short.q: Describe four ways in which a child can stand firm in their Christian faith.
short.answer: Pray, read the Bible, say no to wrong, be proud to be a Christian, join a good church group, ask God for courage.
short.working: 1 mark for each way up to 4.

short.q: Explain how Stephen's forgiving spirit is like that of Jesus and how a child can copy it.
short.answer: Jesus prayed, "Father, forgive them," on the cross. Stephen prayed that the sin would not be held against those who stoned him. A child can forgive those who mock or hurt them, pray for them and not take revenge.
short.working: 1 mark for Jesus, 1 for Stephen, 1 for the similarity, 1 for forgiving, 1 for praying or not taking revenge.

short.q: Write the first two lines of the Lord's Prayer.
short.answer: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. (The wording "who art in heaven" is also accepted.)

short.q: Give two people you should pray for.
short.answer: Parents, guardians, friends, teachers, sick people, leaders.

short.q: Explain the meaning of "Give us today our daily bread".
short.answer: We ask God to give us what we need each day, such as food. We depend on Him and we thank Him for what we have.
short.working: 1 mark for needs, 1 for food or daily, 1 for thanks or dependence.

short.q: State three reasons why we should pray every day.
short.answer: We can thank God; ask for help; grow spiritually; know God better; get strength to avoid wrong.

short.q: Describe four steps of how to pray.
short.answer: Find a quiet moment, speak with respect, thank Him, say sorry, ask for help, say Amen.
short.working: 1 mark for each step up to 4.

short.q: Explain what the Lord's Prayer teaches about forgiveness and protection.
short.answer: We ask God to forgive us as we forgive others, so we must forgive. We ask Him to lead us away from temptation and to deliver us from evil, so we depend on His protection and try to avoid wrong.
short.working: 1 mark for God's forgiveness, 1 for forgiving others, 1 for temptation, 1 for evil, 1 for depending on God.

short.q: Name two fruits of the Holy Spirit listed in Galatians 5:22-23.
short.answer: Any two of love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control.

short.q: Name two fruits of the Spirit and give an example of each.
short.answer: Love: sharing lunch; kindness: helping a friend.
short.working: 1 mark for each fruit with example.

short.q: Explain why Christians should show the fruit of the Holy Spirit.
short.answer: It pleases God, makes us like Jesus, and helps us to live well with others.

short.q: Give three examples of how a child can show self-control at school.
short.answer: Wait for your turn, do not fight, do homework first, do not shout, do not copy.

short.q: Describe four ways of growing the fruit of the Spirit.
short.answer: Pray, read the Bible, practise one fruit at a time, ask for encouragement, say sorry and try again.
short.working: 1 mark for each way up to 4.

short.q: Explain how a child can show any five fruits of the Spirit in daily life.
short.answer: Love: sharing; joy: thanking God; peace: stopping quarrels; patience: waiting your turn; kindness: helping others; goodness: honesty; faithfulness: keeping promises; gentleness: speaking softly; self-control: walking away from a fight.
short.working: 1 mark for each fruit with an example, up to 5.

short.q: Give two signs of a person with self-control.
short.answer: Waits turn, controls anger, shares, saves money.

short.q: Name two things that can defile the body.
short.answer: Alcohol, drugs, harmful media, sex outside marriage.

short.q: Describe three steps for making a right decision.
short.answer: Stop and think, ask if it pleases God, pray, ask advice, choose the right thing.

short.q: Explain the meaning of Proverbs 25:28.
short.answer: A person without self-control is like a city with broken walls, easily attacked and unprotected. Self-control protects us.
short.working: 1 mark for broken walls, 1 for unprotected, 1 for self-control protecting.

short.q: Explain four ways of building self-control.
short.answer: Pray each morning, set small goals, keep busy with good activities, choose good friends, avoid tempting situations.
short.working: 1 mark for each way up to 4.

short.q: Explain what a child should do if they are offered drugs or asked to do something that defiles the body.
short.answer: Say no clearly, walk away, avoid the group, tell a trusted adult such as a parent or teacher, pray for strength, and choose friends who make good choices.
short.working: 1 mark for saying no, 1 for walking away, 1 for telling an adult, 1 for prayer, 1 for good friends.

short.q: Name two digital devices used at home or school.
short.answer: Phone, tablet, computer, TV, radio.

short.q: Give two examples of personal information that you should not share online.
short.answer: Home address, school, phone number, passwords, family photos.

short.q: State three rules for safe use of social media.
short.answer: Ask permission, do not chat with strangers, do not share personal details, be kind, limit time.

short.q: Explain why a Christian should behave well online even when nobody is watching.
short.answer: God sees everything; integrity means doing right in private; good behaviour protects us and others.

short.q: Describe four dangers of misusing social media.
short.answer: Strangers, harmful content, bullying, too much screen time, rumours, sharing private details.
short.working: 1 mark for each danger up to 4.

short.q: Explain what a child should do if a stranger contacts them online and why.
short.answer: They should not reply, should close the chat, should tell a parent or teacher, and can call 116. Strangers may pretend to be someone else and may want to harm the child. Telling a trusted adult keeps the child safe.
short.working: 1 mark for not replying, 1 for closing, 1 for telling an adult, 1 for the helpline, 1 for the reason.
